about: ROUTING-COLLISION table (capreg-2): common owner-style phrasings with the ONE routing group that owns them (plus any group that may legitimately ride along). routingCollision.test.js asserts that no OTHER group's trigger words select the phrase — a group's words stealing another group's everyday language is how CG-12 ('tell me about …' → alerts) and CG-13 ('stack up against' → charts) happened. A known collision carries a gap {id, reason, owner, mode} and must fail in exactly that way.

rows.text: tell me about TSM the company

gap.reason: the alerts words /\b(notify|ping|tell) me\b/ select 'tell me about …'

rows.text: how does NVDA stack up against AMD

gap.reason: the alerts words /\b(notify|ping|tell) me\b/ select 'tell me about …' — and nothing else names data, so the owner group is never sent (SUBTRACTIVE)
the drawings word /\bdraw\w*\b/ selects 'drawdowns' (SUBTRACTIVE: data is not named)

rows.text: how far is NVDA off its high

gap.reason: 'relative strength' is a screener strength word (SUBTRACTIVE: indicators not named)

rows.text: set a price alert on NVDA at 150

gap.reason: 'momentum' is an indicators word, so a saved screen's name pulls the indicators group in (ADDITIVE: budget only)

rows.text: what percent of stocks are above the 50 day

gap.reason: the indicators length word /\d{1,3}[- ]?day/ selects '50 day' in a breadth question (ADDITIVE: budget only)

rows.text: create a new watchlist called Semis

gap.reason: 'swing' is a charts setting word (swing markers), so a layout NAME pulls the charts group in (ADDITIVE: budget only)
'news' is a data word, so a news WIDGET request also routes the data group (ADDITIVE: budget only)
